learn.title: What is an Election?
learn.content: An election is a formal group decision-making process by which a population chooses an individual or multiple individuals to hold public office. Elections have been the usual mechanism by which modern representative democracy has operated since the 17th century.

learn.title: Types of Elections
learn.content: Common types of elections include General Elections (to choose national or state representatives), Primary Elections (to select political party candidates), and By-elections (to fill vacancies that arise between general elections).

learn.title: Eligibility to Vote
learn.content: To be eligible to vote in most democratic countries, you must be a citizen of that country, meet the minimum age requirement (usually 18 years old), and be registered to vote in your specific constituency.

phases.title: 1. Voter Registration
phases.description: Eligible citizens register themselves to be included in the electoral roll.

phases.title: 2. Candidate Nomination
phases.description: Political parties or independent candidates file their nomination papers.

phases.title: 3. Campaigning
phases.description: Candidates present their manifestos and appeal to voters for support.

phases.title: 4. Voting
phases.description: Registered voters cast their ballots at designated polling stations on election day.

phases.title: 5. Counting
phases.description: Votes are systematically counted by election officials.

phases.title: 6. Result Declaration
phases.description: The winner is officially announced based on the highest number of valid votes.
